questions.question: In an out-of-order superscalar processor featuring speculative execution, how does the microarchitecture fundamentally maintain 'precise exceptions'?
options: By deferring exception handling until the faulting instruction reaches the retirement stage at the head of the Reorder Buffer, ensuring prior instructions commit and speculative subsequent instructions can be cleanly discarded.
By halting instruction fetch and decode immediately whenever an instruction with potential fault behavior (such as a load, store, or division) enters the execution pipelines.
By checkpointing the entire physical register file and memory hierarchy to dedicated on-chip shadow registers on every single clock cycle.
By enforcing strictly in-order execution for all arithmetic instructions while permitting only non-faulting memory load operations to execute out of order.
By discarding speculative results and rolling back architectural state immediately when an execution unit signals an exception, without waiting for older in-flight instructions.

questions.question: In a classical pipelined microprocessor (such as the standard 5-stage RISC pipeline), what is the primary operational objective of hardware operand forwarding (data bypassing)?
options: To allow instructions to be fetched and executed speculatively past unresolved conditional branch instructions.
To route an uncommitted result directly from an execution or memory stage to a dependent instruction's ALU input, eliminating pipeline stall cycles caused by read-after-write (RAW) hazards.
To arbitrate structural hazards when instruction fetch and data memory access simultaneously target a single unified cache.
To allow the register file to complete write operations on the falling clock edge while reads occur on the rising clock edge.
To dynamically reorder independent instructions in the pipeline to maximize arithmetic execution unit utilization.

questions.question: In dynamic CMOS logic design, why must a static CMOS inverter be placed at the output of a dynamic gate to create a valid, cascadable 'Domino logic' stage?
options: To restore full rail-to-rail voltage swings because dynamic logic nodes can only charge up to VDD - Vth during the precharge phase.
To invert the boolean polarity because dynamic pull-down networks are physically incapable of synthesizing inverting logic functions.
To satisfy the monotonicity requirement by ensuring that all inputs to subsequent dynamic stages remain low during precharge and only make 0-to-1 transitions during the evaluation phase.
To act as a feedback keeper circuit that prevents subthreshold leakage current from draining the precharged dynamic node over long clock periods.
To decouple the dynamic evaluate network from the precharge clock line, thereby eliminating clock feedthrough and charge injection noise.

questions.question: In multi-clock-domain SoC design, why are the read and write pointers of an asynchronous dual-clock FIFO encoded in Gray code prior to crossing the clock domain boundary?
options: To reduce routing congestion across the floorplan by halving the total number of physical interconnect wires required for pointer transmission.
To eliminate the need for multi-stage flip-flop synchronizers by utilizing the inherent metastability immunity of Gray-coded signals.
To simplify the pointer arithmetic logic because Gray-code incrementers require substantially fewer combinational gates than binary adders.
To guarantee that only one bit changes per counter increment, preventing multi-bit transition skew from producing corrupt intermediate pointer values when sampled by the destination clock.
To allow cyclic redundancy checks (CRC) and parity schemes to perform single-cycle error correction across asynchronous boundaries.

questions.question: In deep-submicron integrated circuit reliability analysis, what physical mechanism fundamentally drives electromigration in on-chip metallic interconnects, and what is its primary macroscopic circuit failure mode?
options: High transverse electric fields causing catastrophic dielectric breakdown between adjacent metal layers, resulting in interlayer short circuits.
Cyclic thermal expansion mismatch between copper lines and the surrounding low-k dielectric, producing mechanical fatigue fractures and trace peeling.
Hot carrier injection into the inter-metal dielectric, leading to gradual parasitic capacitive coupling shifts across neighboring interconnects.
Spontaneous chemical oxidation of copper lines when exposed to sub-surface moisture, creating progressive resistance increases across the chip.

Momentum transfer from high-density conduction electron flux to metal lattice ions ('electron wind'), causing directional mass transport that creates voids (open circuits) and hillocks (short circuits).
